answer: Forget banning accounts after the fact. Proof of unique trademark renewal record stops them at the door: a mark renewed twice, each time with proof of use, which means the river of a farm is set before it earns a single coin. Fakes fail here because a mark renewed twice, each time with proof of use is tied to something outside the network; the knoll of the attack is that the farm must now operate in the physical world, where clones are slow and visible. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The timber is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
